newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stock index falls to seven-month low.
newsitem.headline: Manila stock index falls to seven-month low.

text.p: * Index drops to 2,852.16 points, the lowest in seven months
Manila stocks slumped at the close on Monday, falling rapidly by more than 100 points as the market succumbed to across-the-board selldown, traders said.
"The whole market sympathized with the drop in big cap issues," said Teresa Lee, Lippo Securities assistant vice-president.
The main index finished weaker by 110.44 points, 3.73 percent, to 2,852.16 points.
Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc, said the index last reached a level below 2,850 points on March 29 when the 30-share index was at 2,849 points.
"The market decline started with PNB and other major issues followed," said Reyes. PNB shares fell last Friday on low nine-month earnings triggering selling of the issue.
Traders said secondliners and even tertiary issues suffered falls as they took the cue from major issues.
Losers clobbered gainers 100 to 26 with 47 unchanged issues. All sectors fell except for mining.
Joey Roxas, president of Eagle Securities, said the market may have reached a bottom and may post a 50-point rebound on Tuesday. Traders pegged support at 2,800 to 2,850.
